children: SpaceX (SPCX, Financials) has plenty of ambitious businesses. Pivotal Research thinks one of them matters more than the rest. The firm initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $220 price target, implying roughly 49% upside from recent levels. The core of the call is Starship.

Analyst Jeffrey Wlodarczak believes SpaceX can justify much of its roughly $2 trillion valuation if Starship becomes truly reusable, with each vehicle eventually flying 20 to 50 times and requiring relatively cheap, fast refurbishment between launches.

That would change the economics of spaceflight. Lower launch costs could let SpaceX put Starlink satellites into orbit more frequently, expand the network faster and pursue businesses that would be difficult to justify with expensive launches.
Those could eventually include defense work, space manufacturing and orbital data centers. But there is a catch.
If Starship cannot deliver rapid and inexpensive reuse, Wlodarczak said SpaceX could end up being a much smaller company than investors currently expect.
There is also a more immediate issue. About 319 million SpaceX shares are scheduled to become eligible for sale Sept. 9.
That does not mean all of them will be sold, but it gives existing shareholders another opportunity to take money off the table.

SpaceX therefore enters the week with two very different stories. Wall Street sees substantial long-term upside if Starship works. The market first has to get through another large wave of potential share supply.

title: SpaceX Gets a $220 Target as Starship Reuse Becomes the Big Test
